findings.evidence: L0 routes name actions, but L1 row routes name only semantics and no row resource/action or concealed-denial order.
findings.counter_example: A space-reader denied sensitive decision rows has no deterministic policy outcome.
findings.repair: Define row-list and row-read actions/resources; authorize before family existence, capability, parsing, lookup, and page observations; conceal denial.

findings.evidence: authorization-view digest lacks canonical inputs, policy revision, principal binding, and stability rules.
findings.counter_example: Equivalent policy metadata can invalidate pages, or a principal-only digest can survive revocation.
findings.repair: Bind canonical principal/session, policy revision, action, visible resource set, snapshot, expiry, and protected token; test change/replay/tamper.

findings.evidence: Row list names limit/cursor but only space pagination defines cursor scope.
findings.counter_example: A contexts cursor can be replayed against decisions or a different limit.
findings.repair: Bind row cursor to snapshot, space, family, auth view, last row key, limit, adapter/index version, expiry, and integrity.

findings.evidence: Hash input representations, path encoding/canonicalization, base64url padding, and collision behavior are undefined.
findings.counter_example: Raw digest bytes versus prefixed hex text yield incompatible IDs.
findings.repair: Define byte-exact domain-separated inputs and deterministic vectors; stage 8 additionally replaces this with a secret-keyed random-looking ID.

findings.evidence: No bounds exist for manifest/store/YAML sizes, aliases, depth, parsing time, startup time, or concurrent raw reads.
findings.counter_example: A digest-valid huge ledger or alias expansion can exhaust the process before fail-closed behavior.
findings.repair: Declare configurable hard limits, bounded parsing/streaming, fail-closed codes, and boundary fixtures.

findings.evidence: Problem codes exist without a route-specific precedence through parsing, authz, capability, schema, and lookup.
findings.counter_example: Malformed family syntax on an unauthorized space can leak existence via 400, 409, or 422.
findings.repair: Publish and test a route decision table with transport-safe parsing then authentication, concealed authorization, capability, schema, and lookup.

findings.evidence: Data model says duplicates disable rows and stay internal, while API table exposes ambiguous_row_identity.
findings.counter_example: Implementations can return different 409 codes and leak defects.
findings.repair: Use one caller-visible capability_unavailable response; keep duplicate detail internal unless separately authorized.

findings.evidence: If-None-Match is permitted and 412 is listed, but no explicit snapshot precondition exists.
findings.counter_example: An old ETag can yield 200 or 412 under equally plausible implementations.
findings.repair: Separate ETag revalidation from explicit snapshot pinning; define X-Craft-Snapshot-Match or remove 412.

findings.evidence: No record binds freshness to snapshot, full scope, observer, authorization, observed digests, time, or expiry.
findings.counter_example: A partial or old immutable observation can label a snapshot fresh indefinitely.
findings.repair: Define a complete observation schema/validity predicate; otherwise L0 is always unknown.

survived_attacks: full expected-record closure forbids partial serving
replacement and mutation remain outside requests
residue: OpenAPI, schemas, policy bindings, implementation, and executable tests are absent
reroute: parent design repair then final review
handoff_note: Repair row authorization, cursors, resource ceilings, identifier secrecy, error precedence, preconditions, and freshness validity before plan admission.
